newsitem.title: CHINA: China seen unlikely to import diesel in 2nd qtr.
newsitem.headline: China seen unlikely to import diesel in 2nd qtr.

text.p: China is unlikely to import diesel fuel in the second quarter of this year after a sharp rise in imports and domestic production in recent months, oil officials said on Wednesday.

Industry officials in southwestern Sichuan province said they had been told by Beijing there was no need for further diesel imports in the second quarter. Officials in Beijing, while unwilling to rule out imports, told Reuters that a recent domestic shortfall had been largely resolved.

The Sichuan official, who asked not to be further identified, said Beijing had indicated its stance on diesel imports at a recent meeting organised by the state-run China National Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec).

Sinopec officials in Beijing did not comment directly on the meeting but one company executive said: "Imports from late last year and early this year coupled with increased domestic output have covered the shortfall."
Rising domestic diesel stocks had also caused prices to drop, oil officials said.
In Sichuan province, the market price for diesel fuel has fallen to about 2,700 yuan per tonne, down 314 yuan from the end of last year.
In some parts of the country, diesel had jumped as high as 4,000 yuan a tonne before the imports eased shortages. Diesel was about 2,270 yuan per tonne in August last year.
Sichuan is one of the nation's more remote provinces and is dependent on diesel fuel brought in from other areas. Prices there are often higher than in most other parts of the country.
Diesel stockpiles in the province were 24,000 tonnes by late February, a rise of 60.6 percent from early January, state media said.
China started boosting imports in December and had bought a total of about 1.7 million tonnes of diesel fuel by the end of February, another oil official said.
Beijing also raised the official ex-refinery price of diesel twice in the fourth quarter to stimulate domestic diesel production.
"We had domestic oil refiners boost output to satisfy domestic demand," the Sinopec official said. He did not elaborate.
China produced 3.845 million tonnes of diesel in January, up 12 percent compared with a year ago, official figures show.
Output of diesel in 1996 was 43.25 million tonnes, up 11.2 percent from the year before, official data show.
